items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>claw</radical> kept on the <radical>left-side</radical> and every <radical>measure</radical> taken well in advance is what marks out a <kanji>leader</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: On that same field, Sho the tiny stage magician claps his white gloves, and a dove bursts skyward as the crowd yells <reading>Show</reading>! That's <reading>しょう</reading>, his one trick, performed the same way every time.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Crossing <radical>water</radical> by counting the <radical>degrees</radical> the current pushes you sideways is how you <kanji>transit</kanji> a river.
items.reading_mnemonic: Toto wades into the shallows with a sample door strapped to his shell, testing each stepping stone before he trusts it. Every plant of his foot lands with a flat 「<reading>と</reading>」, like a knuckle rapping a <reading>door</reading>, all the way to the far bank.

items.meaning_mnemonic: An <radical>altar</radical> stands on the left. Beside it, an <radical>eye</radical> lies flat above a line of <radical>ground</radical> — a portrait propped over the offerings. Somebody long dead looks back at you off that shelf: your <kanji>ancestor</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: So is the small catch of sound the incense makes when it takes light at the altar — 「<reading>そ</reading>」 — and for a second the eye in the portrait seems to move. One syllable, once a year, for the ancestor. そ.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Growing one <radical>violet</radical> on nothing but the <radical>power</radical> of habit is what <kanji>diligence</kanji> looks like.
items.reading_mnemonic: Everyone on the trail just calls the porter <reading>Kin</reading> — not his real name, just the sound he wheezes at the summit every morning: a worn-out <reading>きん</reading>. Then he drops the crate and turns straight back down for the next load.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Any <radical>art</radical> that needs a <radical>fire</radical> lit under it is really the art of controlling <kanji>heat</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The clerk mopping her forehead at the register is nicknamed <reading>Netsu</reading> for it. Every time that wall of heat rolls out, she groans her own name, <reading>ねつ</reading>, dragging it out like wading through hot fishing nets.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>wide box</radical> of a room, shoved to the back with <radical>rice</radical> and something <radical>big</radical> on top. You walk through every room to reach it; nobody outside the family does. The deepest room is the <kanji>heart</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ou is the grandmother who lives in that back room and has not come out in years. Knock and you get one long syllable through the paper door — 「<reading>おう</reading>」 — meaning she heard you and no, you may not come in. おう, from the very back of the house.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Hold a match to it, the <radical>fire</radical> takes, and <radical>so it is</radical> settled that the whole thing will <kanji>burn</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The neighborhood kids call Grandma Kane <reading>Nan</reading>, and when the incense flares she comes flying out stamping sparks off the mossy steps, yelling the cat's name so fast it comes out <reading>ねん</reading>. Picture Nan hollering ねん at that cat, and the reading burns itself in.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Let the same thing <radical>pierce</radical> your <radical>heart</radical> often enough and you will get <kanji>accustomed</kanji> to it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Behind the counter, Koichi restocks the drink case so many times his hand does it alone — each can lands with a flat clink that sounds like <reading>かん</reading>, someone saying <reading>khan</reading> without the h. He's stopped hearing it. That's how accustomed he's become.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>mouth</radical> that can talk a drawn <radical>sword</radical> back into its sheath knows perfectly well how to <kanji>seduce</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Backstage, Sho takes his bow, and the crowd gasps <reading>しょう</reading> in unison — one long <reading>show</reading> of a breath. He tips his tiny top hat, and that gasp is the only applause a magician his size ever needs.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>cult</radical> and your <radical>elder brother</radical> finally agreeing on something is reason enough to <kanji>celebrate</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The coach gets <reading>shook</reading> so hard by the shoulder-ride that his whistle flies into the bleachers. <reading>しゅく</reading>! <reading>しゅく</reading>! the players chant with every shake — and a second later, he tips backward into the equipment cart.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A messenger who can <radical>run</radical> faster than the <radical>warrior</radical> chasing him will <kanji>surpass</kanji> him inside a mile.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the summit, a hiker named <reading>Etsu</reading> collapses against the vending machine and groans <reading>えつ</reading> between gasps — the same groan echoes down the trail every time someone else finally surpasses that last ridge.

items.meaning_mnemonic: An <radical>assembly</radical> that has to be held halfway up a <radical>hill</radical> tells you the ground there is <kanji>precipitous</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Guarding that narrow ledge is <reading>Ken</reading>, the shiba who never leaves his wall of antique swords. Every hiker who nears the edge gets one warning bark of <reading>けん</reading> before he bares a blade in his teeth.
items.description: Beyond the literal steep-cliff picture, this kanji usually carries a broader sense of danger or risk in real vocabulary — insurance, adventure, hazard — rather than physical steepness itself.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A single <radical>step</radical> turns into a wild <radical>run</radical> down the road. There is no horse or cart anywhere in sight. So the whole trip happens <kanji>on foot</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Toto the door-to-door turtle has never once taken a ride. He carries the sample doors on his shell and walks the entire round, and he announces himself at every house with the same syllable before he knocks — 「<reading>と</reading>」. と, and another mile.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>shelter</radical> you can <radical>extend</radical> every time more people turn up is what gives everybody <kanji>ease</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: For once Koichi sits down under that roof, feet up on a crate, and lets out one long yawn: <reading>こう</reading>. He stretches out like someone sighing a slow <reading>kaaah</reading> into the rain, and doesn't move again for ten minutes.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Two feet walking down a <radical>hill</radical> is the plainest way there is <radical>to descend</radical>, so the character just means <kanji>descend</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi treks up that same trail himself to restock the vending machine. When the last case slips from his arms and crashes down every step behind him, he just sighs 「<reading>こう</reading>」 — more <reading>cough</reading> than word — and watches it disappear downhill.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>woman</radical> handed a <radical>sweeper</radical> the moment she walks in is being called a <kanji>lady</kanji> to her face.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the shrine gate, Fumi leans her broom against the rail and blows out a long <reading>phew</reading> — a breathy 「<reading>ふ</reading>」 that scatters the incense smoke. Then she picks the broom up to finish the steps.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>woman</radical> sweeps her yard with a <radical>broom</radical> tied to a <radical>stick</radical>. She works until the bare <radical>ground</radical> is spotless. The neighbors call her the tidy <kanji>wife</kanji> of the house.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sai is the one who actually decides. Ask her husband anything and he glances sideways at her first; she gives one flat 「<reading>さい</reading>」 and that is the answer on behalf of both of them. さい settles it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>sheep</radical> dragging its whole <radical>body</radical> up the <radical>road</radical> makes every journey behind it <kanji>slow</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The class hamster, <reading>Chi</reading>, is let loose to race him and loses on purpose, wheezing one flat unimpressed <reading>ち</reading> at the finish line — same track, same dragging in dead last.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A young <radical>woman</radical> reaches the door, ready to leave. A strict house rule ends up <radical>stopping</radical> her before nine. She sighs and stays inside, still somebody's <kanji>daughter</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Jou is how the neighbours refer to her, drawn out and a shade too formal — 「<reading>じょう</reading>」. It is the address for a girl of good family who is not allowed out tonight. She hears じょう and rolls her eyes.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>hole</radical> cut so a lonely <radical>heart</radical> can see out of its <radical>cocoon</radical> is exactly what a <kanji>window</kanji> is.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the same konbini, a raccoon dog crashes through the new opening chasing a dropped onigiri and skids across the tile. The clerk can only gasp 「<reading>そう</reading>」 — that flat English <reading>so</reading> of someone watching it happen with no better word for it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> kneels on the wet <radical>ground</radical> as <radical>rain</radical> pours down. A clerk presses his <radical>stamp</radical> on the puddle, and the ink washes away. Nothing is left to count, so he writes <kanji>zero</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Rei is that clerk. She is scrupulously polite about it — a small bow, a murmured 「<reading>れい</reading>」 — and then she inks the nothing into your row and moves down the line. れい, bow, zero. She has done it forty times today.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>sun</radical> on the left has been let off: the shape on the right squeezes from under the heavy lid, walking off <radical>exempt</radical>. Its shift is done; it drops below the roofline unbid. The sun excused from duty: <kanji>nightfall</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ban is the night watchman who takes over the moment the sun clocks off. He drags the gate shut and announces himself to the empty street — 「<reading>ばん</reading>」 — one flat syllable, every night, so you know the day is closed.
